newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn settles lower on exports, crop estimate.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn settles lower on exports, crop estimate.

text.p: Corn futures on the CBOT ended lower Friday, in response to a slow weekly export sales pace and bearishly interpreted crop estimates from a widely-watched advisory firm, some floor traders said.
On Friday, the U.S. Department of Agriculture reported corn export sales of 447,000 tonnes, which was below trade expectations of 450,000 to 600,000 tonnes.

The private advisory firm, Sparks Cos, of Memphis, Tenn. pegged the final 1996 U.S. corn crop at 9.295 billion bushels, which was 30 million higher than USDA's latest estimate of 2.265 billion and considered slightly bearish for futures, traders said.
Others disagreed and said that the Sparks estimate had no influence on prices because projections about the anticipated estimate were factored into trading on Thursday.
There were also rumors circulating on the trading floor that China sold 70,000 bushels of corn for export, but no confirmation of the business could be immediately obtained, traders said.
CBOT corn futures closed down 1/4 to two cents per bushel, with March down two at $2.56-1/2 a bushel and May down two cents at $2.59.
